decisions.reason: A newly launched handle family in a firm with long-lived, coordinated design ranges is very unlikely to be withdrawn within a year of launch.
Mitred lever families take years of specification work with architects to pay off, so an early withdrawal would waste the tooling and planning investment.
A multifunctional handle fits the firm's push into barrier-free and system solutions, which argues for keeping it.
Single handle models are cheap to keep listed in the catalogue, and German architectural hardware makers seldom drop new designs this quickly.
The award-winning FSB 1289 collection has its own web page and strong design recognition, making it a flagship to keep.
A finish option uses the firm's in-house finishing know-how across many products at low incremental cost, so it is likely to stay.
